context: Al-Muddaththir belongs to the same early period as Al-Muzzammil, and the authentic reports place its opening among the first revelation after a pause. Jabir ibn Abdullah relates that the Prophet ﷺ described seeing the angel again after that interval, becoming frightened, returning home and asking to be covered, and that this was then revealed.

Where the other surah told him to stand and pray, this one tells him to get up and warn, and to make his garments clean and to leave what is filthy. It is the point at which private preparation becomes public work. Its later section deals with a specific man who heard the Qur'an, was moved by it, and then constructed a reason to dismiss it.
name_story: Al-Muddaththir, the Cloaked One or the One Covered Over, from the first verse. It pairs with Al-Muzzammil deliberately: the same man, the same blanket, two different commands. The naming preserves the moment before the mission became public.

movements.note: Get up and warn, magnify your Lord, purify your garments, avoid what is filthy, and do not give in order to receive more. The whole commission in seven short lines.

movements.h: The man who thought and measured
movements.note: The account of a man given wealth and sons who considered, then decided, and called the Qur'an magic transmitted from before. Then Saqar, and the nineteen over it.
The oaths, and the answer given by those inside: we were not of those who prayed, nor did we feed the poor, and we used to talk idly with those who talked idly.
The image of frightened donkeys fleeing a lion, the demand that each of them be handed his own scripture, and the closing statement that this is a reminder for whoever wills.

themes.d: The command changes from stand and pray to arise and warn, and the surah marks the exact point at which the mission left the house.
Do not give, seeking to gain more. Placed inside the commission itself, which locates sincerity at the start rather than as a refinement.
The man in this surah does not fail to understand. He thinks, and measures, and reaches a conclusion he has decided in advance, and the surah reports his deliberation in detail.

themes.t: Four reasons given by those inside
themes.d: Not praying, not feeding the poor, idle talk, and denying the Day. Two of the four are omissions rather than acts.

heart: Recited slowly, the seven opening lines read like a job description. Arise. Warn. Magnify your Lord. Purify your garments. Avoid filth. Do not give expecting return. Be patient for your Lord. Nothing in it is abstract and the whole of a prophet's public life is contained in it.

The answer given by those in Saqar is what stays with most readers, because two of the four things they name are not crimes. We were not of those who prayed, and we did not feed the poor, and we used to talk idly. It is a list of things not done.

passages.why: Arise and warn. The commission in seven lines, including the instruction not to give in order to receive more.
What put you into Saqar? They will say: we were not of those who prayed, nor did we feed the poor. A list of omissions.
Every soul, for what it has earned, is retained. One clause that closes off every argument about inherited standing.
None knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. Said in the middle of the passage about the nineteen, and it settles the matter.

connections.why: Al-Muzzammil addresses the same man in the same blanket and tells him to pray; this one tells him to go out and speak.
Al-Alaq holds the first five verses ever revealed, and this surah records what followed the pause after them.

virtue.text: No authentic report establishes a specific merit for reciting Al-Muddaththir. What is authentically reported is its occasion: Jabir ibn Abdullah relates the Prophet's ﷺ own account of seeing the angel after the pause in revelation, returning home frightened, asking to be covered, and this surah then being revealed.
virtue.src: no authentic virtue report; the occasion in Bukhari 4922 and Muslim 161
